Closes the remaining Appendix C type-safety work items (T2.1 remainder, T2.2, T3.1), enforces the PRD §1.3.7 90% coverage gate, and syncs changeset-level documentation. No re-implementation of the framework; R2-R4 are type-only (the only runtime-touching exceptions are T2.2's identity helper and T3.1's internal type reuse), and the coverage gate is cleared by ADDING tests, never by weakening the threshold.

milestones.title: Type-safety completion (R2, R3, R4)
milestones.description: Finish the remaining Appendix C work items: T2.1 strict key-checking on <Form<TFieldValues>> config + generic <Field name>, T2.2 opt-in defineInputs helper, T3.1 exported FormalityFieldComponentProps. All type-only / additive; core stays framework-agnostic (no react/react-hook-form dependency); generic defaults preserve today's behavior.

tasks.title: Finish T2.1 — strict FormProps.config keys + generic FieldProps
tasks.description: Close the strict key-checking half of Appendix C T2.1. (1) Re-parameterize ReactFormFieldsConfig<V> so unknown config keys on <Form<TFieldValues>> are rejected, while the default FieldValues collapses to today's string-keyed Record (non-breaking). (2) Make FieldProps generic over the field name (FieldProps<TName extends string = string>), defaulting to string so <Field name={anyString}/> still compiles. Audit internal call sites; add a type-level assertion that an unknown config key fails to compile.

subtasks.title: Key-check ReactFormFieldsConfig<V> against TFieldValues
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/002_78ea74508dd8/architecture/type_system_state.md §1. packages/react/src/overlays.ts:72-76 currently defines `ReactFormFieldsConfig<V extends FieldValues = FieldValues> = Record<string, ReactFieldConfig<V>>` — the key set is UNBOUNDED. Form.tsx:48 uses `config: ReactFormFieldsConfig<TFieldValues>`. Core already has `FormFieldsConfig<TName extends string = string> = Record<TName, FieldConfig>` (config.ts:130-133). The gap is purely on the react overlay side. CRITICAL: when V = FieldValues (the default), `Extract<keyof FieldValues, string>` MUST collapse to `string` so today's `Record<string, ...>` behavior is byte-for-byte identical (non-breaking, per Appendix C.3).
2. INPUT: The existing `ReactFieldConfig<V>` overlay (overlays.ts:61-65) and the `FormProps<TFieldValues>` interface (Form.tsx:43-71). No new core types needed.
3. LOGIC: Implement PRD Appendix C T2.1 step 1 (REACT). Edit packages/react/src/overlays.ts: change `ReactFormFieldsConfig<V>` to `Record<Extract<keyof V, string>, ReactFieldConfig<V>>`. Do NOT touch core. Verify Form.tsx:48 (`config: ReactFormFieldsConfig<TFieldValues>`) now rejects unknown keys when TFieldValues is a concrete type, and still accepts any string key when TFieldValues is the default FieldValues. Audit every internal usage of ReactFormFieldsConfig / FormProps in packages/react/src (grep) — Form.tsx:48 is the only field-type usage; transformValuesForSubmit (Form.tsx:715) uses the CORE FormFieldsConfig (default string) and must stay untouched. Add explicit type arguments ONLY where inference breaks. Mock: none (pure type change).
4. OUTPUT: A narrowed `ReactFormFieldsConfig<V>` exported from @formality-ui/react (and re-exported via index.ts) such that `<Form<ClientValues> config={{ ofice: {...} }} />` is a compile error while `<Form config={{ anyString: {...} }} />` still compiles. Consumed by Form.tsx:48 and by downstream consumers like sellario-ui.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Add/update JSDoc on `ReactFormFieldsConfig<V>` in overlays.ts noting it now rejects unknown config keys when TFieldValues is narrowed. No separate docs subtask — this rides with the work.

subtasks.title: Make FieldProps generic over the field name
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/002_78ea74508dd8/architecture/type_system_state.md §3. packages/react/src/components/Field.tsx:40-66 defines a NON-generic `interface FieldProps { name: string; ...; [key: string]: unknown; }`. The destructure at Field.tsx:115-124 is `function Field({...}: FieldProps)`. FieldRenderAPI (Field.tsx:69-85) is also non-generic. Per Appendix C T2.1 (and delta R2), FieldProps must become `FieldProps<TName extends string = string>` with `name: TName`. The default TName=string keeps `<Field name={anyString}/>` compiling unchanged (non-breaking). Leverage prior research: plan/001_bbf464589edd/docs/research/typescript_interface_extension_best_practices.md (backward-compatible generic interface patterns).
2. INPUT: The narrowed `ReactFormFieldsConfig<V>` from P1.M1.T1.S1. The existing FieldProps interface (Field.tsx:40-66) and its index signature `[key: string]: unknown`.
3. LOGIC: Implement PRD Appendix C T2.1 step 2 (REACT). (a) Change `export interface FieldProps` to `export interface FieldProps<TName extends string = string>` and `name: string` to `name: TName`. KEEP all other members and the `[key: string]: unknown` index signature (additive). (b) Update the Field function signature to carry the generic: `export function Field<TName extends string = string>(props: FieldProps<TName>): JSX.Element | null`. (c) If a clean non-breaking per-form name-linkage is feasible without internal churn, optionally narrow Field's name against the enclosing Form's TFieldValues; if it proves risky, SCOPE this subtask to FieldProps generic only and note it (Appendix C T2.1 explicitly permits dropping per-form name-linking if a clean thread is impossible). (d) Add a TYPE-LEVEL assertion test (a .ts file using `@ts-expect-error` on `<Field name="typo" />` inside a typed Form context, or an `Expect<Equals<...>>` helper) proving an out-of-union name fails to compile, AND that the default `<Field name={anyString}/>` still compiles. Audit internal call sites (Field.tsx:124, any tests) and add explicit type args where inference breaks. Mock: none.
4. OUTPUT: A generic `FieldProps<TName=string>` exported from @formality-ui/react and used by the Field component, defaulting to string (identical runtime + compile behavior to today), with a passing type-assertion test. Consumed by the Field component and by downstream consumers.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Add JSDoc on `FieldProps<TName>` noting the name is checked when narrowed by a typed `<Form<TFieldValues>>`. Rides with the work; no separate docs subtask.

tasks.title: Add opt-in defineInputs helper (T2.2)
tasks.description: Add and export the identity helper defineInputs<T extends Record<string, ReactInputConfig>>(inputs: T): T so consumers can wrap provider inputs and derive an InputType = keyof typeof inputs union, making FieldConfig.type / <Field type=...> typos (e.g. 'texField') a compile error. Pure identity (tree-shakes to nothing in production). Additive only — existing non-generic Field/FieldConfig.type stays unchanged.

subtasks.title: Implement and export defineInputs identity helper + test
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/002_78ea74508dd8/architecture/type_system_state.md §4 & §8. `defineInputs` does NOT exist anywhere in packages/ (grep-confirmed). packages/react/src/index.ts has a 'React Type Overlays' section (last) exporting `ReactInputConfig, ReactFieldConfig, ReactFormFieldsConfig` from './overlays'. `ReactInputConfig` (overlays.ts:42-49) is the right input-element type. Per Appendix C T2.2 / delta R3: defineInputs is a pure IDENTITY function — it returns its argument unchanged with zero runtime effect, so tsup tree-shakes it to nothing. It exists purely so consumers can write `const inputs = defineInputs({...})` and derive `type InputType = keyof typeof inputs`.
2. INPUT: The existing `ReactInputConfig<TValue>` overlay (overlays.ts:42-49), already exported. The provider `inputs: Record<string, ReactInputConfig>` used by FormalityProviderProps (FormalityProvider.tsx) and ConfigContextValue.
3. LOGIC: Implement PRD Appendix C T2.2 (REACT, the one item permitted to add a tiny runtime helper). (a) In packages/react/src/overlays.ts add: `export function defineInputs<T extends Record<string, ReactInputConfig>>(inputs: T): T { return inputs; }`. (b) Export `defineInputs` as a VALUE export from packages/react/src/index.ts (it is a function, not a type — add to the overlays export section but use `export { defineInputs }`, not `export type`). (c) Add JSDoc with the `InputType = keyof typeof inputs` usage example from Appendix C T2.2, noting it is opt-in and the default non-generic `Field`/`FieldConfig.type` is unchanged. (d) Add a unit test asserting: (i) defineInputs returns its input referentially (`expect(defineInputs(x)).toBe(x)`), and (ii) a type-level assertion that `keyof typeof result` is the expected union (e.g. 'textField' | 'switch') and that a typo'd key is rejected. Mock: none (pure identity). Do NOT change Field or FieldConfig.type defaults.
4. OUTPUT: An exported `defineInputs` factory from @formality-ui/react; consumers can wrap provider inputs to get compile-time keyof checking on input type keys. Bundle size unchanged (identity inlined by tsup).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on `defineInputs` (the InputType derivation example). Rides with the work; no separate docs subtask.

subtasks.title: Define, export, and internally reuse FormalityFieldComponentProps
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION: 1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/002_78ea74508dd8/architecture/injected_props_types.md (the authoritative source for the three prop types). Verified runtime types: (a) formState = `UseFormStateReturn` — RHF Controller render arg (react-hook-form@7.68.0 controller.d.ts:24-31), already used at Field.tsx:82 & types.ts:25. (b) forwardRef = RHF `RefCallBack` = `(instance: any) => void` — Field.tsx:421 sets `coreProps.ref = field.ref` and Field.tsx:451 spreads it; RHF controller.d.ts:14-18, form.d.ts:125. NOTE spelling: RHF uses `RefCallBack` (capital B). (c) state = `CustomFieldState | Record` — NOT injected at runtime today (provideState/passSubscriptions config knobs exist in core FieldConfig config.ts:146-154 but are unconsumed in Field.tsx); the type reflects the INTENDED contract from examples/07-advanced-features.tsx:67-99 and CustomFieldState (types.ts:30-58). Field.tsx:426 currently casts `inputConfig.component as React.ComponentType` (discards prop typing). CONSTRAINT (Appendix C.3 / delta R4): new export only, no existing API changed, RUNTIME UNCHANGED — wiring state/formState into coreProps for bare components is a separate FUTURE task, out of scope here. 2. INPUT: The existing `CustomFieldState` (types.ts:30-58, already exported), RHF types (`RefCallBack`, `UseFormStateReturn`, `FieldValues`). The Field.tsx render layer (Field.tsx:393-460). 3. LOGIC: Implement PRD Appendix C T3.1 (REACT). (a) In packages/react/src/overlays.ts (or a small adjacent module) define and export `export type FormalityFieldComponentProps

= P & { state?: CustomFieldState | Record; formState?: UseFormStateReturn; forwardRef?: RefCallBack; }` importing CustomFieldState from ./types and RefCallBack/UseFormStateReturn/FieldValues from react-hook-form. (b) Reuse internally: change the Field.tsx:426 cast to `inputConfig.component as React.ComponentType` (keeps the type in sync by construction; NO behavior change — it is still an `as` cast). (c) Export FormalityFieldComponentProps as a TYPE from packages/react/src/index.ts (overlays section). (d) Optionally re-export RefCallBack/UseFormStateReturn/FieldValues from @formality-ui/react so consumers don't need a direct react-hook-form import. (e) JSDoc MUST: instruct component authors to destructure `state`, `formState`, `forwardRef` OUT before forwarding the rest to the underlying DOM input (avoid leaking to DOM); call out the MUI v9 `slotProps={{ input: { ref: forwardRef } }}` pattern (PRD §5.3.8); and note the runtime caveat that Field currently delivers ref via the React-special `ref` key (forwardRef-typed consumers wrap with React.forwardRef or use React 19 ref-as-prop). (f) Add a test asserting react's OWN field components (and a representative test input component) satisfy FormalityFieldComponentProps (compile-time), plus that the type is exported. Mock: none (type-only + one cast). 4. OUTPUT: An exported `FormalityFieldComponentProps

` from @formality-ui/react that replaces consumer hand-rolled `WithFormality

` helpers (the driving consumer sellario-ui can drop FormalityInjectedProps/WithFormality); reused internally in Field.tsx so the contract cannot drift. Runtime unchanged. 5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on FormalityFieldComponentProps (the three injected props + stripping guidance + MUI v9 slotProps note). Rides with the work; no separate docs subtask.
